candidates.name: trial01
candidates.note: At ordinary boundaries, require persistent poor observed goal progress and nearby fixed blockage; select a rectangle-face bypass and steer one pusher to the appropriate station. Release after the planned object displacement or a bounded timeout. Full-start 13/22, with 2 rescues and 3 losses.

candidates.name: trial02
candidates.note: Prioritize P’s accepted elective bypass and avoid overriding its solo approaches or global repositioning. Permit intervention during a new stalled target command or for a staged singleton using a direction already proposed in a joint push. Source exceeded the 48 KiB cap. Rejected at source validation before any rollout.

candidates.name: trial03
candidates.note: Prioritize P’s accepted elective bypass and avoid overriding its solo approaches or global repositioning. Permit intervention during a new stalled target command or for a staged singleton using a direction already proposed in a joint push. Full-start 16/22, with 2 rescues, 0 losses, and a later success in 126.

candidates.name: trial04
candidates.note: Commit a bypass only after its first command executes. Add a fallback for sustained near-zero pusher speed and fixed blockage along its actual visible face, allowing a nearby orthogonal slide when the geometric margin is tight. Full-start 14/22, with 2 rescues and 2 losses.

candidates.name: trial05
candidates.note: Causally commit after action feedback. When a bypass pusher maintains contact and recently moved the object along its axis but goal range has barely improved, extend that legal push briefly if its observed swept corridor remains clear. Require a forward component when replacing an engaged joint push. Full-start 16/22, with 2 rescues, 0 losses, and 126 at tick 1791.

candidates.name: trial06
candidates.note: After a confirmed local displacement and a return to P, allow up to two follow-up stationing attempts if object progress stalls again. Keep the original narrow entry gate for the first intervention. Full-start 16/22, with 2 rescues, 0 losses, and 126 at tick 1550. Selected.

candidates.name: trial07
candidates.note: At a contact or travel checkpoint during a previously stalled joint drive, drop an unready teammate only when the engaged robot has a legal singleton and a better observed fixed-obstacle corridor. Keep checkpoint memory disposable. No additional accepted action change on the development panel relative to trial05.

candidates.name: trial08
candidates.note: Give a newly contacted pusher a bounded grace period after a long stationing approach, provided its original action remains legal and the visible corridor is open. Same development-panel outcomes and accepted boundary actions as trial06.
